title.title: Positively curved Einstein 4-manifolds are the three models
title.subtitle: Claim: a closed Einstein 4-manifold with $\sec > 0$ is round $S^4$, round $\mathbb{RP}^4$ or Fubini–Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$

plain: Four-dimensional spaces curved positively and evenly in every direction are only the three textbook shapes

nodes.label: curvature parallel, so a symmetric model

beats.text: A volume argument forces the two Weyl blocks to have equal second moments
Exact polynomial certificates then force one block to vanish
Then the curvature is parallel, and the manifold is one of the models

steps: Balance the two halves of the curvature: equal second moments
An exact polynomial inequality then forces one half to vanish
So the curvature is parallel and the space is a standard model

A polynomial inequality forces one half to vanish, leaving the symmetric models.
Claimed: round sphere, projective space, or Fubini Study.

sources.quote: Closed Einstein 4-manifolds with positive sectional curvature are, up to scaling, round S^4, round RP^4 or Fubini-Study CP^2 (Yang's conjecture)
Every earlier result needed extra pinching or topology (Gursky–LeBrun, Cao–Tran, Gursky–Malchiodi)
a volume argument forces their second moments to be equal
moment balance and exact polynomial sign certificates force one Weyl block to vanish, then the curvature is parallel and the manifold is a model
The positive-curvature classification is in Lean (`OAI/Geometry/EinsteinFour`, about 209,000 lines, the largest formalization in this group)
which openly takes that classification as a stated assumption, are paper-only

I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read
